probes.question: Hello Mr Graham, I'm Dr Patel, one of the emergency doctors on tonight. Is it alright if I ask you some questions?
probes.target: OPEN
probes.credits: Introduced yourself by name and role

probes.question: When did this pain first start?
probes.target: How long you have had the pain: since 8 o'clock last night, so about a day now. It is 9 at night now.

probes.question: Had you eaten anything just before it came on?
probes.target: It began a few hours after a Chinese takeaway at 6 yesterday evening.

probes.question: Can you show me exactly where it hurts most?
probes.target: The pain is in the upper right side of your stomach, under the ribs. Say "It is right here, under my ribs on the right side."

probes.question: Does the pain spread anywhere else, like your back or shoulder?
probes.target: It also goes through to your right shoulder blade.

probes.question: What does the pain feel like to you?
probes.target: The pain is dull, not sharp. It hurts more when you take a deep breath.

probes.question: Is it there the whole time, or does it ease off in between?
probes.target: It never goes away. It is constant.

probes.question: Is there anything you've found that helps it, or anything that sets it off more?
probes.target: Nothing makes it better. Lying still helps a little. Nothing makes it worse.
probes.credits: What makes it better or worse

probes.question: If ten is the worst pain you can imagine, how bad is it now?
probes.target: Severity: 8 out of 10.

probes.question: Have you been feeling sick or throwing up?
probes.target: You feel sick to your stomach. Yes, that is nausea. The smell or even the thought of food makes it worse. You have not vomited.

probes.question: Have you felt hot or had any shivering spells?
probes.target: You feel like you have a fever right now. In the waiting room you had shaking chills and could not stop shaking. You say this with feeling.

probes.question: Has anything like this ever happened to you in the past?
probes.target: You have had this pain twice before. Six months ago after dinner, lasting three hours, and again two weeks ago after a lunch party. Both were milder. Neither came with a fever.

probes.question: When you open your bowels, have you noticed any change in the colour of what comes out?
probes.target: (only if asked) Your stools have been a lighter colour than usual. Pale, like clay. Not black.

probes.question: And when you go for a pee, what colour has it been?
probes.target: (only if asked) You last passed water this afternoon. It was dark, almost like tea. No blood in it.

probes.question: Do you take any regular medicines?
probes.target: You take two inhalers for asthma, flovent and albuterol, and Synthroid for an underactive thyroid. Nothing else. No over the counter medicines. No street drugs.

probes.question: Is there anything in particular that's worrying you about all this?
probes.target: (only if asked) You are frightened of needing an operation.

probes.question: Have you had any diarrhoea?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Have you travelled abroad recently?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Have you lost any weight without trying lately?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Have you ever had an operation on your tummy?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Is there anything else you think I should know?
probes.target: OPEN
